title: Anthropic ships a Claude commerce-agent blueprint with Shopify and Visa
subtitle: The reference stack pairs a consumer shopping agent with a merchant operations agent, and open-sources the harness that made carts up to 35% larger in early pilots.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Anthropic on September 2 published a blueprint for building commerce agents on Claude — a bundle of reference implementations, guardrails, and evaluation harnesses that Anthropic says lets an engineering team put an agent into production in days rather than months. The company followed up on September 3 by open-sourcing the reference code across retail, travel, telecom, and entertainment use cases. Two agents anchor the blueprint: a consumer agent that searches, compares, and adds items to a cart, and a merchant agent that manages inventory, pricing, and marketing on the other side of the transaction.

The launch matters because it moves Anthropic from selling a model to shipping the pattern for a category. Early users named in the announcement include Shopify, Visa, Mastercard, and Accenture, and Anthropic reports that retailers running shopping agents on Claude have seen carts up to 35% larger and shoppers 60% more likely to complete a purchase. A companion plugin for Claude Code ships alongside the blueprint so developers can scaffold the two-agent setup directly from the CLI.

Agentic commerce has been a moving target for the last year — Visa and Mastercard have both published their own agent-payment specs, OpenAI has wired ChatGPT into checkout flows, and Shopify has rolled out merchant-side agents. Anthropic's move is to package the whole shape of the workflow, from consumer prompt to merchant fulfillment, as a working template on Claude. It follows the same play Anthropic ran with Claude Code: give teams a reference implementation that already works, and let the platform effects build from there.

Takeaway for learners: the interesting artifact here is not the model, it is the blueprint. When a lab ships a reference implementation of a full agent workflow — with the guardrails, evaluations, and second-side agent already wired in — the barrier to production drops from a research project to a code copy. That is how a category standardizes, and it is worth studying the blueprint itself as a design document even if you never plan to ship a shopping agent.
